function: Joint BS beamforming (communication and sensing), RIS element positions and RIS phase shifts for near-field ISAC, maximizing weighted sum rate under a CRB sensing constraint (p. 3-6).
system: Near-field ISAC at 30 GHz: BS with M=8 fixed antennas, reflecting RIS with N=16 movable elements, Kc=5 communication users, Ks=3 sensing targets (Table I, p. 7).
method: Unsupervised (label-free loss): CNN on 8x8 user-location grids plus dense heads for antenna positions, beamforming, RIS phase; trained end-to-end with Adam on -WSR plus CRB penalty (p. 5-6).
data_channel: Simulated near-field spherical-wave channels from geometry; users and targets randomly placed in a 5 m square at (15, 15, 0); no standardized model or dataset (p. 3-4, 7).
test_conditions: No separate test set or shift stated; random user positions in one area; sweeps over transmit power, movement range, sensing users, communication users, RIS elements (p. 7-9).
baselines: Non-learned: alternating optimization (AO) of positions, beams and phases; fixed-position antennas (FPA); random RIS phases (RPM). Learned: none (p. 7).
metrics: Weighted sum rate (bps/Hz) versus transmit power, MA region size, numbers of users and RIS elements; array gain pattern; channel gain map (p. 7-9).
complexity: Analytical complexity orders per step, dominant term O((Kc+Ks)MN + Kc^2 M + Ks^2 M + M^2 N); no runtime or parameter count (p. 6-7).
q1_support: p. 3: "Under near-field conditions, the propagation of the signal follows the spherical wave model". Missing: any 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data; the channel is a custom geometric spherical-wave model (p. 3-4).
q2_support: p. 9: "Fig. 8 evaluates how the number of RIS elements N affects" the rate, with "for a certain number of training batches". Missing: any test of a trained model in a configuration not used for training; sweeps only.
q3_support: p. 7: "Alternating Optimization (AO): For AO,"; "FPA: For FPA, we assume that the antennas at both the BS and the RIS are fixed in place"; "RPM: For RPM, the phase shifts of the RIS are randomly". Missing: any earlier learned method as baseline.
q4_support: p. 7: "the step-wise computational complexity of Algorithm 1 is analytically characterized in Eq. (23), where the dominant term F is given by Eq. (24)"
q5_support: p. 7: "The communication users and sensing targets are randomly distributed within a square region of 5 meters, centered at (15, 15, 0)". Missing: any code or data link or DOI; the results come from the authors' own simulation.
notes: Area 5 (beamforming in an ISAC system with a CRB sensing constraint); area 3 loses to area 5 by the order of specificity. Eligibility kept because a trained network (CNN plus dense heads) outputs the beams, phases and positions with a label-free loss (p. 5-6); the text does not state the number of training samples or whether the network is trained per user layout (Algorithm 1 loops until convergence for given positions, p. 6), so the reviewer may check how far the model generalizes. q4 counts only the analytical complexity orders of Algorithm 1 (Eq. 23-24, p. 6-7); the paper claims reduced computational overhead but reports no runtime or parameter count. In q3, FPA and RPM are restricted configurations (fixed antenna positions, random RIS phases), not earlier learned methods. Pages count the 11 pages of the file.
